facts.text: The only player of the 1940s to gain 1,300 yards from scrimmage: Gene Roberts, 1949 — 1,345 scrimmage yds.
The only player of the 1940s to average 46 yards a punt (40+ punts): Joe Muha, 1948 — 47.3 avg on 57.
Only two players of the 1940s rushed for 1,000 yards: Steve Van Buren (2×, best 1949: 1,146 yds); Tony Canadeo (1949: 1,052 yds).
Only two players of the 1940s carried the ball 200 times: Steve Van Buren (3×, best 1949: 263 carries); Tony Canadeo (1949: 208 carries).
The only player of the 1940s to gain 1,000 receiving yards on 50 or fewer catches: Jim Benton, 1945 — 1,067 yds on 45 rec.
The only player of the 1940s to record 2 safeties: Willie Wilkin, 1942 — 2 safeties.
Only two players of the 1940s ran for 10 touchdowns: Steve Van Buren (4×, best 1945: 15 rush TD); Bill Paschal (1943: 10 rush TD).

Just three players of the 1940s averaged 22 yards a catch (30+ catches): Ken Kavanaugh (1947: 25.6 per catch, 32 rec); Jim Benton (1945: 23.7 per catch, 45 rec); Mal Kutner (2×, best 1948: 23 per catch, 41 rec).

method: NFL before 2000: each line is one Stathead (Pro Football Reference) Season Finder query over the decade, run in a signed-in subscriber session; the result rows, with Pro Football Reference's stable player ids, are stored as provenance. Nothing recalled or estimated.

Passing, rushing and receiving are official from 1932, interceptions from 1940, sacks from 1982 (Pro Football Reference's unofficial earlier sack counts are excluded); rules on a category a decade did not record simply return nothing. The 1960s include AFL seasons, which NFL records count; the 1940s exclude the AAFC, which they do not.
